# Jo — Style Profile

*Compiled October 2026. Consolidates the wardrobe project, colour analysis, styling rules, inventory and buying plan.*

---

## 1. Aesthetic direction

**The formula:** masculine base → feminine signal → hard gold → warm accessory.

Sits between refined and bohemian. Completely considered. One focal point per outfit. Quality fabrics. Gold jewellery doing the work.

**Primary shopping filter:** *does it read expensive?* Judged on fabric, finish and hardware — never on platform or original price.

**Current direction (from Sept 2026):** evolving toward a more creative, elevated, Trinny-Woodall-adjacent style — colour confidence and statement tailoring. Introducing statement, unexpected and investment pieces so the wardrobe reads less exclusively high-street, while staying climate-appropriate for Abu Dhabi. Equal weight on the no-spend route: restyling what's already owned in unexpected ways (dress over trousers, shirt over slip, cropped over high-rise, breaking up co-ords).

---

## 2. Physical context

- Based in Abu Dhabi — hot most of the year, heavily air-conditioned interiors
- Age 50
- 187cm — tall, slim, athletic frame with strong/broad shoulders
- Olive, warm-toned skin
- Short dark hair with a silver streak
- Hardware is **gold** throughout

**Implications:** can carry scale, volume, long lines and drama. Cowl, halter and deep-V necklines flatter the shoulders. Wide-leg balances the frame. With a strong athletic frame and silver hair, deliberate feminine signals are non-negotiable to avoid an androgynous read.

> **Height confirmed: 187cm** (October 2026). The bottoms rule below was originally calibrated to 177cm, so judge crop lengths against 187cm: a hem that hits the ankle bone on a shorter model will sit higher on me.

---

## 3. Colour

### Core 10 (warm autumn)

olive green · sand/camel · chocolate · terracotta/rust · forest green · sage · charcoal (warm grey) · soft near-black · steel navy · deep navy

### Approved add-ins

- **Shale green** (khaki/olive family)
- **Burnt sienna** — deep terracotta; the cowl-top colour
- **Lava-falls tomato red**
- **Teal** — ONE piece only
- **Muskmelon warm orange** — bag/scarf accent only

### Confirmed exceptions

- White / cream / ecru — works well despite sitting outside the strict warm palette; especially when tanned
- Hot-pink halter — occasion only, when tanned
- Brick-red ribbed tee
- Blue/white stripe shirt, worn with warm accessories

### Avoid

Fuchsia · cobalt · lilac · pale yellow

**The rule:** if it reads cool, pale or sweet, it isn't hers.

**Palette discipline:** strict warm-neutral near the face; relaxed at the extremities. Cool bags or cuffs are acceptable; cool tops are not.

---

## 4. Silhouette and styling rules

### The bottoms rule (critical)

Trousers must be either **full-length and fluid** (unbroken vertical line) **or**, if cropped, **narrow/tapered at the ankle bone**. Stiff + wide + cropped-at-calf is permanently banned. The ~4-inch difference between lower calf and ankle bone is the entire difference between mumsy and deliberate.

### The barrel jean filter

Narrow barrel at ankle bone = acceptable. Wide crop at any length above the ankle bone = banned. Judge crop length and leg width strictly before buying.

### The sleeve ban

Cap sleeves and puff/balloon sleeves are non-negotiable exits. Any option must clear this filter first. Shoulders: sleeveless, halter, cowl, or clean short sleeve only.

### Proportion

Fluid top + clean bottom. Never both voluminous. One unbroken vertical line.

### One focal point

One statement element per outfit. If the bottom is the focal point, top and accessories stay restrained — and vice versa.

### Register rule

Dressy and casual fabrics cannot mix. A piece is locked to the register of its cheapest element. Linen and satin combine only when both occupy the same formality register — there, texture contrast reads as strength.

### Placed embellishment

Vertical or placed embellishment dictates the silhouette — can't belt or tuck through it. It has to work as-is; side-seam tailoring is the only rescue, never belting.

### Navy with black

Allowed when deliberate: clear shade gap, contrasting textures, one colour as a single block. Avoided when both are similar weight and finish — reads accidental.

### Kaftans

Worn with stark modern accessories, to avoid a costume read.

---

## 5. Feminising signals

Non-negotiable, given the frame:

- Substantial gold jewellery — statement pendant, chunky cuffs
- Delicate, elegant footwear even with masculine trousers — never chunky
- Fitted or cropped feminine tops under looser layers
- Defined waist, through belting or tucking
- Soft fabrics against tailored ones (broderie, fine linen)
- Warm colours near the face
- Styled bags — suede, straw, gold-woven. Never plain black

---

## 6. Fabric

**Fabric-first.** Linen, satin, crepe, fluid jersey. Nothing stiff or synthetic.

**Target for future trousers:** viscose/polyamide blend — lightweight, matte, drapey, breathable. The H&M olive pair is the reference point. Not satin-finish, not linen blend.

---

## 7. Jewellery and accessory rules

- Gold is the metal
- **One-statement rule:** one gold cuff OR earrings — not both
- **One-bag rule**
- Owns 5 gold sculptural cuffs; the orange/magenta striped clutch is the single focal statement piece

## 11. Keeps with restrictions

- **Black beaded kaftan** — evening slot only
- **Green embroidered kimono** — beach register only. Right colour, wrong voice (gauze and dainty floral). Serves as the "before" reference for the forest-green abaya search.
- **Tan lace-up espadrilles** — elevated-casual only, never with tailoring
- **Dark brown raffia hobo** — casual register only
- **Splash broderie shirt** — soft casual register; not structured enough to read expensive. Let elevation come from tailoring, leather and satin instead.
- **H&M olive viscose/polyamide trousers** — casual register. Do not pair with crisp tailoring like the Zegna shirt.

## 13. Buying plan

**Budget ceiling: AED 600 per piece.** This shifts elevation sourcing away from Massimo Dutti's top end toward COS and & Other Stories — best fabric and fit at the price. Real leather trousers and true-silk pieces sit above the ceiling.

**Footwear is the main gap.** Currently only slides and trainers; needs elevated leather shoes — a good sandal plus a closed flat or mule.

### Priority order

1. Pointed leather flats or mules — the one missing register, highest priority
2. Terracotta cowl-neck satin top — unlocks four combinations
3. Chocolate or deep-navy wide-leg trouser
4. Substantial gold pendant on leather cord
5. Tan/cognac leather belt
6. Forest-green or terracotta plain open abaya (CAS Basics)
7. Warm silk neck scarf
8. Brown full-length fluid trousers
9. Narrow-ankle barrel jeans — judged strictly against the barrel filter
10. Terracotta viscose resort shirt
11. Broad leather-strap watch

**Already well stocked — don't rebuy:** black satin and black wide-leg trousers, linen shirts (blue/white/black), cream satin co-ord.

**Abaya search direction:** forest green or terracotta. Nida, crepe or cotton blend. Open front works well for the frame. Blazer or kimono silhouette. Restrained — no heavy embellishment, no sequins.

## 15. How to work with this

- Reference the actual inventory and rules above — not generic styling advice
- Direct product links, not search terms or instructions to go looking
- Flag honestly when a retailer genuinely can't deliver a specific fabric, then reframe before redirecting
- Keep records accurate; accumulated inventory errors are the known failure mode
- Direct, precise, detail-oriented. Overly restrictive assessments get pushed back on.
